_: What the King can do about a piece of news (news_actions.gd; Crusader Kings 3's alert with its answers, Warcraft III's 'our town is under attack'). kinds: a news kind (the chronicle's kind, or 'attack' for a foe's host on one of the King's towns, which news_actions.gd sees in the realm itself) -> its verbs, left to right; any other kind takes 'other'. Each verb is an order the King already has (a host order, a decree, the court, the tithe), never a new one; a verb with 'decree' in its row is that decree, placed by its row (at: town|seat; town: mine|theirs|any; not_seat; building + built_as, offered only where the town lacks it; unsworn: only a house not sworn to the crown), and one with 'ui' is the King's own control (ui.gd counsel_act: court, tithe_down, tithe_up). Every kind that reaches the news has at least one answer; notice: the kinds that are the King's own doings told back, or the year's turn, with nothing to decide (they keep only Go there): defend (the nearest free royal host garrisons the town: POST /host/order through host_command.gd), levy (the decree 'Raise the royal levy', mustered at Kingsmere), grain (the decree 'relief'), feast (the decree 'feast' in the town's lord's honour), rule (opens its matter at court), go (the camera to the town; Space or Home brings it back). A verb shows only where it fits (defend and levy at the King's own towns, grain and feast at a town, rule when a matter waits). verbs: each verb's words; its price is the bridge's (decrees.json via /world). free_orders: the orders a royal host may be taken from to defend. attack_hold: how long a threat's line stays in the corner, seconds (other lines: the ticker's 14). threat_words: the line for each threat ({house}, {town}). The kinds also cover the scenes the camera captions (scene_kinds.gd: siege, storm, razed, famine, plague...): a caption over a scene carries the same row (news_chips.gd caption). relief: the decree 'relief' as for grain, named for a sickness. caption_seconds: how long a caption with answers stays up. Now first (2026-11-16, Mac: 'The Siege of Rosehall' offered Call the banners after its plague had passed): a card's answers are, best first, the Hand's advised decree; a court matter's own answers (answers_most of its options, in the court's order; Rule on it stays only when they don't all fit); states: what the place's state asks now, each 'when' a key of the mirror (threat: a foe's host on this royal town; besieged; hungry: starved, granary low or the siege biting; plague; unrest: disorder; crown_war: the town's house at war with the crown, crown_word in its wars; cold: its house's favour under cold_below; war: realm-wide, the crown at war or threatened); the title's theme only when no state speaks; then the kind's list. no_state: kinds whose cards never take the place's verbs (good news, notices). verbs.needs: a verb shows only while one of these keys holds. gift: the decree 'gift' (a small chest of crowns). truce: the decree 'truce' (the King's herald makes peace with a house at war with the crown). threat_kinds: kinds whose own list stands before the place's states (a rising: the levy before a feast). states[].skip: kinds a state's verbs don't join (a cold lord's gifts on a raid). A raid on a house's town not at war with the crown is a threat too (news_actions.gd _realm_town): Defend sends the nearest free host to advance on it (attack-move); the levy musters at Kingsmere whoever's town it is. fresh_seasons: a threat kind's card about a town of the realm counts as a threat there for this many seasons after its news (Defend and the levy answer it), whoever's men they are. court_waits: a matter waits at court now (court_panel.gd waiting()); To court shows only then.
